arguments.command:
python3 - << 'PY'
# Data from page 17 - in thousands of dollars
# Individual and Corporation columns under "Income and profits taxes"

jan_individual = 20561
jan_corporation = 25128

feb_individual = 43443
feb_corporation = 27503

mar_individual = 356076
mar_corporation = 298548

# Calculate ratios (individual / corporation)
ratio_jan = jan_individual / jan_corporation
ratio_feb = feb_individual / feb_corporation
ratio_mar = mar_individual / mar_corporation

print(f"January 1940: {ratio_jan:.6f}")
print(f"February 1940: {ratio_feb:.6f}")
print(f"March 1940: {ratio_mar:.6f}")

# Now do linear regression: months (1, 2, 3) vs ratios
import statistics

x = [1, 2, 3]
y = [ratio_jan, ratio_feb, ratio_mar]

# OLS: slope = sum((x-xbar)*(y-ybar)) / sum((x-xbar)^2)
xbar = statistics.mean(x)
ybar = statistics.mean(y)

numerator = sum((x[i] - xbar) * (y[i] - ybar) for i in range(len(x)))
denominator = sum((x[i] - xbar)**2 for i in range(len(x)))

slope = numerator / denominator
intercept = ybar - slope * xbar

print(f"\nLinear Regression:")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f}")
print(f"Slope rounded to thousandths: {round(slope, 3)}")
PY
